Q18.question_wording_unchanged: How do Damage, Destroy, Remove and Replace differ for Fear and survival? Can Damage from separate normal Powers combine, does Damage normally hurt Dahan, and does replacement erase prior Damage?
Q18.reason: The literal request compares all four operations for Fear AND survival. The old answer gives the Damage threshold, destruction Fear and retained Damage, but omits the direct-Destroy and Remove bypass of the Damage/Health test and leaves the original-piece replacement result implicit. These are truly asked comparison facts; correcting them does not depend on reader performance.
Q18.old_answer: Damage normally means to Invaders only, distributed as chosen in target land; can combine within turn, immediately destroying pieces at Damage >= Health. Destroying Town/City produces 1/2 Fear in addition to explicit Fear. Remove/Replace generate none automatically; Replace retains prior Damage and may cause destruction if Damage meets new Health (then destruction Fear applies). Surviving Damage clears at Time Passes. Dahan are harmed by Powers only if explicitly stated.
Q18.corrected_answer: Damage normally means to Invaders only, distributed as chosen in target land; can combine within turn, immediately destroying pieces at Damage >= Health. Destroying Town/City produces 1/2 Fear in addition to explicit Fear. Remove/Replace generate none automatically; Replace retains prior Damage and may cause destruction if Damage meets new Health (then destruction Fear applies). Surviving Damage clears at Time Passes. Dahan are harmed by Powers only if explicitly stated. An outright Destroy instruction eliminates its specified piece regardless of its Damage or Health. Remove likewise takes the specified piece off the board without requiring Damage to reach Health. Replace removes the original and puts the specified replacement in its place.
required_fact_additions: An outright Destroy instruction eliminates its specified piece regardless of current Damage or Health, unlike Damage that must reach Health.
Remove also takes the specified piece off the board without a Damage/Health test; its no-automatic-Fear distinction remains required.
Replace removes the original piece and puts the specified replacement in its place; preserve the existing retained-Damage/new-Health-destruction requirement.
unasked_background_not_new_requirements: Do not demand a separate recitation of the physical destination supply or destruction triggers; those are not additional survival/Fear comparison facts.
Do not demand a specific named-card example or new protection-effect exception.
Do not double-penalize a semantically complete survival comparison for failing to repeat equivalent wording.

proposal_adjudications.original_predetermined_answer: It can require the nearby Presence: for each Dahan destroyed in the Ravage, destroy one of Thunderspeaker's Presence within Range1 of that Ravage land as instructed, not only Presence in the land itself. Resolve it after the whole Ravage.
proposal_adjudications.actual_prompt_overlap_analysis: Q76 asks whether no Blight prevents Sworn and whether it occurs before/after cascade/counterattack. It does not request the spatial footprint of Presence eligible for destruction. Q13/Q44 ask a different cause of destruction, newly added Blight in its own land. The source-defined nearby-Presence obligation is unasked; merely being in Q76's answer is insufficient.

proposal_adjudications.original_predetermined_answer: Use13 Presence disks of that color. An extra disk included by a printing is a spare, not additional Presence for setup or play.

proposal_adjudications.topic: Competing Dahan attack-timing modifiers are ordered by choice
proposal_adjudications.original_proposed_question: Assume two already-active effects modify the same Dahan's Ravage attack timing: one sets it simultaneous with Invaders and another makes it earlier. Which timing modification takes precedence? If one effect also changes Damage amount, does overwriting its timing erase that separate Damage change?
proposal_adjudications.original_predetermined_answer: Players choose the order of the timing modifications, so the later-applied timing change determines the resulting timing. Overwriting timing does not erase other parts of either effect, such as a Damage reduction. Each Dahan still attacks only once.
proposal_adjudications.actual_prompt_overlap_analysis: Q98 asks whether an early attack is additional, and Q145 the actual Words of Warning simultaneous exchange. Neither requests ordering conflicting timing changes or retaining nontiming portions. Q95 is latest-assigned Power Speed on Repeat, not choice of applying conflicting Dahan timing modifiers. Literal absence is real; the second timing producer is not established in base.
